title: Global EV sales reach 2.09 million units in October 2026
gist: Global EV sales hit 2.09M in October 2026 (+8% YoY, -3% MoM), with YTD at 17.5M (+5%). Europe's BEV-led growth (+36% YoY) and a booming Rest of World offset a shrinking Chinese domestic market that is exporting record NEV volumes, while the US has reset to a smaller post-tax-credit base.

insights.claim: Global EV sales (BEV+PHEV, passenger and light duty) were 2.09 million units in October 2026, up 8% year-on-year but down 3% month-on-month, per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Global EV demand has returned to positive YoY growth, supporting battery material demand assumptions.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, specialising in EV

insights.claim: Year-to-date 2026 global EV sales reached 17.5 million units through October, only 5% above the same period of 2025, signalling a sharp slowdown in global EV growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Single-digit global EV growth undercuts bullish lithium/battery demand forecasts built on 20%+ growth.
insights.quote: Year-to-date sales now stand at 17.5 million units, up 5% on the same period last year.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Data Manager, Charles Lester

insights.claim: Regional divergence defines the 2026 EV market: Europe is up 31% YTD and Rest of World up 93% YTD, while China is down 11% YTD and North America down 21% YTD.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Battery/material demand growth is now driven by Europe and emerging markets, not China or the US.

insights.claim: European EV sales were 510,000 units in October 2026, up 36% year-on-year, running ahead of the 31% year-to-date growth pace, which indicates momentum is still building.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Europe is the strongest major-market growth engine for EV and battery demand going into 2027.
insights.quote: Growth is still building, with the monthly year-on-year rate continuing to run ahead of the year-to-date pace

insights.claim: In Europe, battery electric vehicle sales rose 49% year-on-year in October 2026 while plug-in hybrid sales rose only 7%, so growth is skewed heavily toward BEVs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: BEV mix shift raises battery kWh per vehicle and thus cathode/lithium intensity of European demand.

insights.claim: Germany's EV penetration exceeded 45% of new car sales in October 2026, the highest since December 2022, with German BEV sales up almost 80% year-on-year to more than 95,000 units.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Germany's recovery after its 2023 subsidy cliff shows European BEV demand can stand on its own.
insights.locator: Germany recorded its highest EV penetration

insights.claim: UK EV sales grew 30% year-on-year in October 2026 despite comparing against a base already supported by the Electric Car Grant, suggesting underlying demand strength rather than subsidy-driven growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Growth against a subsidised base is a higher-quality demand signal than subsidy-led spikes.

insights.claim: Portugal's EV penetration reached 55% in October 2026, placing it among the most electrified car markets in Europe.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Southern European markets are reaching Nordic-like penetration, broadening the European demand base.

themes.theme: US market reset after tax credit expiry

insights.claim: North American EV sales rose 24% year-on-year in October 2026 to 130,000 units, the region's first annual increase of 2026, but this mostly reflects an easier comparison base rather than a demand recovery.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Headline YoY growth in North America is a base effect; investors should not read it as a recovery signal.
insights.quote: North America returned to year-on-year growth for the first time this year, but this is not an entirely positive story.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Data Manager, Charles Lester

insights.claim: After the US federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September 2025, US EV sales collapsed and have since stabilised at around 110,000 units per month, effectively resetting the US market to a smaller base.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: US EV/battery demand assumptions (and US cell plant utilisation) should be anchored to a structurally lower post-credit base.
insights.quote: the US market has stabilised at a lower level rather than recovered

insights.claim: The North American EV year-to-date decline narrowed to 21% at end-October 2026 from 24% at end-September, as comparisons begin to lap the post-tax-credit collapse.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: YoY comps will look better into 2027 purely mechanically; underlying volumes matter more.
insights.locator: The North American EV market returned

themes.theme: China: shrinking home market, record exports

insights.claim: China's EV sales were 1.14 million units in October 2026, up 5% month-on-month but down 12% year-on-year (narrowed from -18% in September), leaving the market down 11% year-to-date.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The world's largest EV market is contracting in 2026, a major drag on global battery demand growth.
insights.locator: The Chinese EV market’s year-on-year decline

insights.claim: EV penetration in China hit a new high because the wider passenger car market is falling more steeply than EV sales, meaning EVs are gaining share of a shrinking domestic market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Rising penetration in China masks absolute volume decline; share metrics can mislead on demand.
insights.quote: EVs continue to take a growing share of a shrinking domestic car market
insights.locator: The Chinese EV market’s year-on-year decline

insights.claim: With domestic demand subdued, Chinese manufacturers have maintained production and pushed exports, with passenger car NEV exports reaching almost 600,000 units in October 2026, a monthly record up from 558,000 in September.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese overcapacity is being exported, intensifying price competition and trade friction in overseas markets.

insights.claim: Chinese NEV exports face 2027 policy headwinds: an EU cap on imports of Chinese-built hybrids and a cut in China's VAT export rebate for NEVs from 13% to 9% from 1 April 2027.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Export-led relief for Chinese automakers may weaken in 2027, likely pulling exports forward into Q1 2027.
insights.quote: the reduction in China’s VAT export rebate for NEVs from 13% to 9% from 1 April 2027

themes.theme: Rest of World boom and its fragility

insights.claim: Rest of World EV sales rose 85% year-on-year to 300,000 units in October 2026, leaving the region up 93% year-to-date, making it the fastest-growing region.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Emerging markets are becoming a material incremental demand source, largely served by Chinese brands.
insights.locator: Sales in the Rest of the World

insights.claim: Australia's EV sales rose more than 200% year-on-year in October 2026, but a surge of new, largely Chinese, car brands is fragmenting sales and squeezing dealer margins, so volume growth is not translating into healthy dealer profits.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese brand proliferation drives volume but erodes downstream profitability in import markets.
insights.quote: this growth has not translated into healthy profits for dealers
insights.locator: Australia’s EV sales were up more

insights.claim: Brazil's 2026 EV boom was driven largely by temporary factors—imports pulled forward ahead of phased tariff step-ups, a fuel crisis boosting EV demand, and BYD's local plant ramp—and its growth drivers look set to ease once tariffs are fully in place and fuel prices normalise.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Expect Brazil's EV growth to decelerate sharply; BYD's local production becomes the main remaining support.
insights.quote: After this period of extreme growth, the drivers of Brazil’s EV market look set to ease.
insights.locator: Brazil has also seen huge growth

insights.claim: BYD's local Brazilian plant will also serve Argentina and Mexico, positioning it as the main structural support for Latin American EV supply once Brazil's tariff and fuel-driven tailwinds fade.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: BYD's localisation in Brazil creates a tariff-insulated Latin American export hub.
insights.locator: Brazil has also seen huge growth
